pages.text: The $(item)MoE Routing Rack$() is the open camp's $(bold)central deployment hub$(): insert an $(item)Open-Weight Module$() from a pretraining run and the model becomes resident in cluster memory, with downstream routing configured from here.$(br2)It never bills Tokens — open-camp compute comes out of your own machine room.

pages.title: The 5×5×5 Stepped Structure
pages.text: $(li)$(#0E7490)y=0$(): the heavy $(item)Computer Casing$() base plate carrying the energy, item and maintenance hatches.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=1$(): the deployment console, controller front-centre at $(bold)(2, 1, 0)$(); the deployment slot and the four LoRA slots live in the GUI.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=2$(): the routing core — $(item)Cleanroom Glass$() around an $(item)Advanced Computer Casing$() spine.$(li)$(#0E7490)y=3$(): the re-widened shoulder; $(bold)y=4$() steps in as the roof heat ring.

pages.title: Loading, OOM and Going Offline
pages.text: After a module is inserted the router asks the cluster pool for the TB the model declares:$(li)Pool is big enough → $(bold)ONLINE$(): the model is resident and bills CWU/t per tick.$(li)Pool is short → $(bold)OOM$(): the load is $(bold)refused$() and not a single CWU/t is charged.$(br2)$(bold)Pulling the card, pulling an HBM module, darkening a memory rack or a chunk reload$() all take the model offline on that very tick (EVICTED/EMPTY) — it never shows online while the memory is already gone.

pages.title: LoRA Extensions and DeepThink
pages.text: $(bold)LoRA extensions$(): a model with four LoRA slots (Qwen 9187) takes the 0.2.1 $(item)Mining LoRA Card$() or $(item)Chemical LoRA Card$(), each costing $(bold)+4 TB$() and $(bold)+4 CWU/t$() and stacking its by-product specialisation.$(br2)$(bold)DeepThink$(): models with the charge switch (DeepSeek-V6767 Pro) reserve an extra $(bold)+16 TB$() and force probability by-products to $(bold)100%$() — mining cobalt goes from 1/3 to guaranteed, and the scrubbing tower's golden samples get a floor.$(br2)Either can push VRAM past the pool, so stock the TB first.

pages.title: Cloning a Copy
pages.text: Open-camp master weights can be cloned cheaply in the $(item)Micro Burner$(): one $(item)High-Purity Domain Dataset$() plus one $(item)Blank Carrier$() presses out a fresh $(item)Open-Weight Module$(), so a second machine room never has to re-run 2400 ticks of training.
